THE ANCHOR DECISION, stated because it is load-bearing and the step did not fix it. The window is anchored on the NEWEST PROBE, not on a wall clock. Reasons: (i) this module is documented "Projection only" and owns no clock - `deriveHealthState` beside it is likewise clock-free, and injecting `Date.now()` would make the projection untestable without fake timers and make the served frame depend on request time; (ii) a ring that went quiet three days ago still shows its final recorded hour rather than an empty chart, and `lastProbe.at` is what tells the operator how stale that hour is. Documented on the member so no consumer infers a wall clock. Boundary is INCLUSIVE of the far edge (`at < oldestAllowed` drops), the natural reading of "the last hour"; step 3 pins that with an exactly-at-the-edge arm.

Newest-LAST ordering preserved by filtering in source order rather than re-sorting, so `latencySeries.points.at(-1)` and `lastProbe` cannot disagree about which end is newest.

FAIL-CLOSED ON UNPARSEABLE INSTANTS: an unparseable NEWEST instant yields an empty series (never a NaN-bounded slice that would silently keep everything); an individual unparseable instant is DROPPED rather than carried, because a NaN travelling into a chart renders as nothing, which looks identical to a gap nobody recorded. This is the daemon-side half of the NaN discipline DoD 4 asks for on the client.

THE SIX SERIES ARMS:
1. DoD 1 - a ring spanning NINETY MINUTES at one probe a minute (91 rows, asserted generated: `expect(ring).toHaveLength(91)`, so a sweep that silently yielded zero cases cannot pass). Asserts windowMinutes 60, COUNT 61, points[0] == the 10:30 instant, points.at(-1) == the 11:30 instant, and that points.at(-1).at equals lastProbe.at. 61 not 60 because the far edge is inclusive - both endpoints of a closed hour.
2. Window edge - probes at newest-60m-1ms, newest-60m and newest; asserts exactly [2,3] survive, so inclusivity is pinned in both directions in ONE arm.
3. Empty ring -> `{points: [], windowMinutes: 60}` by toEqual, never null: an absent/null member would make "brand new" indistinguishable from "unreadable" at the client's exact-key gate.
4. Single-probe ring -> a one-point series (the client's one-point degenerate input, pinned at the source).
5. ANCHOR arm - a ring from 2019 still plots its final hour. This makes the newest-probe anchor OBSERVABLE rather than an implementation detail, and it is why the plan's "ring entirely older than the window yields an empty series" arm does not exist: under a newest-probe anchor the newest row is always its own anchor, so that state is unreachable. planningNotes.risks:
THE TEST THAT PASSES WHILE THE WINDOW IS BROKEN. DoD 1 names this precisely: a projection that returns the WHOLE ring passes any test that only checks the newest point. The windowing arm must feed a ring SPANNING MORE THAN AN HOUR and assert BOTH the returned COUNT and the OLDEST RETURNED INSTANT. The same trap on the client side is why DoD 4 asks for the plotted point count — a sparkline drawing 1440 points looks fine to a test that only checks that an SVG rendered.

DEGENERATE INPUTS ARE DAY-ONE INPUTS, not edge cases: a brand-new environment has ZERO probes. Zero points must render the empty state and emit NO NaN in any SVG attribute (a NaN in a `points` or `d` attribute renders as nothing and passes a test that only asserts the element exists — assert the ATTRIBUTE VALUES). One point must not divide by a zero range, and neither must all-identical latencies, which is the same divide reached by a different route. Assert the three SEPARATELY as DoD 4 requires; one combined arm cannot say which broke.

THE DERIVATION TEMPTATION IS THE POINT OF THE ROW'S FIRST RAIL. Handing the browser a latency series is exactly what invites recomputing UP/DEGRADED/DOWN from it. The existing disagreeing-frame arm in `environments-section.test.tsx` is the guard; it must pass UNWEAKENED, and DoD 6's drill (recompute the state from the new series) must RED it. If the drill does not redden, the guard is not load-bearing and the arm needs fixing before the row can complete.

ADDING THE KEY REDS THE CLIENT DECODER BY DESIGN. Do not reach for a subset match (task rail 3). DoD 3 requires stating that the red was SEEN before the fix, because that observation is the only evidence the exact-key discipline is real rather than asserted.

ASCII-ONLY, APOSTROPHE-FREE JSX TEXT (task rail 5): an apostrophe in JSX reds the scheduler package-boundary scan in a distant lane, so it will not be caught by this row's own gates.
